2.zh: 模型对齐作为前景理论优化

2.text: Although it is impossible to say that HALOs are categorically better than non-HALOs, we find that among existing methods, those that meet the definition of a HALO work better than those that do not (§3.3). We find that DPO performance can even be matched at most scales by running an offline PPO variant on dummy +1/-1 rewards, suggesting that preference data might not be needed if the inductive bias in the loss function is good enough. However, despite the surprising success of this simple baseline, it significantly lags behind DPO at the 30B LLM scale and suffers from hyperparameter sensitivity, making it difficult to use. Taking a more principled approach, we derive a HALO using the model of human utility that Kahneman & Tversky proposed to describe how humans make decisions about uncertain monetary outcomes (Tversky & Kahneman, 1992). This approach, which we call Kahneman-Tversky Optimization (KTO), directly maximizes the utility of generations instead of maximizing the log-likelihood of preferences, as most current methods do (§4.1). KTO only requires a binary signal of whether an output is desirable or undesirable for an input. This data is more abundant, cheaper, and faster to collect in the real world, making it easier to scale alignment in production and rapidly iterate on models. We find that:

2.text: The intent behind KTO was that even if the model learns from a weaker signal, we could compensate with the higher volume of data that could be accessed in practice; the fact that KTO can match and even outperform DPO on the same data is thus surprising. We conclude by discussing some theoretical explanations for this phenomenon (§4.4). Despite the success of KTO in our experiments, our work ultimately suggests that there is no one HALO that is universally superior; the best HALO depends on the inductive biases appropriate for a given setting, and this choice should be made deliberately instead of defaulting to any one loss.
2.zh: KTO 的本意是：即便模型学到的信号更弱，也可以用实践中能够获取的更大数据量来弥补；因此 KTO 能在同一份数据上追平甚至超过 DPO，这一点令人意外。我们最后讨论这一现象的若干理论解释（§4.4）。尽管 KTO 在实验中很成功，我们的工作最终表明，并不存在一种普遍更优的 HALO；最好的 HALO 取决于给定场景下合适的归纳偏置，这个选择应当有意为之，而不是默认用某一种损失。

5.text: The surprising success of offline PPO with dummy +1/-1 rewards suggests that—with the right inductive biases—a binary signal of good/bad generations may be sufficient to reach DPO-level performance, even if the offline PPO approach itself was unable to do so past a certain scale (§3.3). Taking a more principled approach, we now derive a HALO using the Kahneman-Tversky model of human value, which allows us to directly optimize for utility instead of maximizing the log-likelihood of preferences.

7.text: We find that the performance of an aligned model is more sensitive to the learning rate than any other hyperparameter. The optimal learning rate for KTO is usually 2x to 10x the optimal learning rate for DPO; since the reference-adjusted reward tends to be much smaller in magnitude for KTO, one needs to use a more aggressive learning rate to compensate. For example, the default learning rate for DPO at the 8B parameter scale is 5e-7 (Rafailov et al., 2023), but we find that a default of 5e-6 works best for KTO across all setups (with SFT, without SFT prior, when using an already instruction-tuned model, and when using LoRA instead of full finetuning). When using smaller or larger models, it is recommended to use a smaller or larger learning rate accordingly. In general, if the learning rate is too aggressive, then the implied rewards of both desirable and undesirable examples will decline; ideally, only the latter should decline, with the former staying flat or increasing. 9.text: KTO was designed with the motivation that even if binary feedback were weaker, one could compensate with sheer volume, as such data is much more abundant, cheaper, and faster to collect than preferences. 10.text: The existence of HALOs raises many questions. For one, KTO is based on the Kahneman-Tversky value function for monetary gambles, which is almost certainly different from how humans perceive the relative goodness of text. What value functions and reference point distributions best describe how humans perceive language, and how do they vary across domains and individuals? How can we identify the best HALO for each individual and setting instead of using one default loss? On a more technical level, important directions include developing HALOs that: (1) incorporate granular feedback, such as a score, especially when optimizing for multiple desiderata; (2) work for other modalities (e.g. images) and model classes (e.g., diffusion models), especially models that do not produce an explicit distribution over the output space; (3) can resolve contradictions in feedback according to different definitions of fairness; (4) are designed to be used with online data, where the direction of feedback is implied by rθ or some external reward data. Ecologically valid evaluation (De Vries et al., 2020), where the aligned models are deployed in real-world settings, is also needed to judge the merits of different HALOs.
10.zh: HALO 的存在引出许多问题。其一，KTO 基于的是金钱赌局上的 Kahneman-Tversky 价值函数，这几乎肯定不同于人类如何感知文本的相对好坏。什么样的价值函数和参考点分布最能描述人类如何感知语言，它们又如何随领域和个体变化？如何为每个个体和每种场景找出最好的 HALO，而不是使用一个默认损失？在更技术的层面上，重要方向包括发展这样的 HALO：（1）纳入细粒度反馈，例如分数，尤其是在同时优化多项要求时；（2）适用于其他模态（如图像）和其他模型类（如扩散模型），尤其是那些不在输出空间上给出显式分布的模型；（3）能按不同的公平定义来消解反馈中的矛盾；（4）设计成与在线数据一起使用，此时反馈方向由 rθ 或某种外部奖励数据所暗示。还需要生态效度意义上的评测（De Vries et al., 2020），把对齐后的模型部署到真实场景中，才能判断不同 HALO 的优劣。

10.text: Informally, say there are two contradictory preferences over the output for x, with the majority p preferring ya and the minority 1 − p preferring yb. In the worst-case, when p is sufficiently low and the reference model is sufficiently unaligned, the optimal DPO policy is more likely to produce the minority-preferred output yb even though the DPOimplied reward ranks the majority-preferred output higher: rθ(x, ya) > rθ(x, yb). In contrast, the KTO update rule will increase the relative likelihood of the majority-preferred ya if the value function is loss-neutral (λD = λU), which is the default setting. This suggests that KTO has better worst-case outcomes when handling feedback intransitivity.
10.zh: 非正式地说，假定对 x 的输出存在两条互相矛盾的偏好，多数派比例 p 偏好 ya，少数派比例 1 − p 偏好 yb。在最坏情况下，当 p 足够低且参考模型足够不对齐时，最优 DPO 策略更可能生成少数派更偏好的输出 yb，即便 DPO 所隐含的奖励把多数派更偏好的输出排得更高：rθ(x, ya) > rθ(x, yb)。相反，若价值函数是损失中性的（λD = λU），这也是默认设置，KTO 的更新规则会提高多数派更偏好的 ya 的相对似然。这表明在处理反馈的不可传递性时，KTO 有更好的最坏情况结果。

10.text: Although model alignment has historically been rewardcentric, we found that the inductive biases of alignment objectives are critical to their success. Moreover, these inductive biases have analogs in the prospect theory literature, suggesting that they work in part because they reflect human biases in decision-making. We abstracted these insights into a family of alignment objectives called human-aware losses (HALOs). We then proposed a HALO called KahnemanTversky Optimization (KTO) for directly maximizing the utility of generations instead of maximizing the likelihood of preferences, as existing methods do. Despite only learning from a binary signal of whether an output is (un)desirable, KTO was as good or better than preference-based methods in our experiments. More broadly, our work suggests that akin to how there is no one reward model that is universally superior, there is no one loss function either—the best HALO depends on the inductive biases that are most appropriate for a given setting, and much work remains to be done in identifying the best HALO for each context.
10.zh: 尽管模型对齐历来以奖励为中心，我们发现对齐目标的归纳偏置对其成功至关重要。而且这些归纳偏置在前景理论文献中有对应物，说明它们之所以有效，部分是因为反映了人类决策中的偏差。我们把这些认识抽象成一族称为人类感知损失（HALO）的对齐目标。然后我们提出一种叫 Kahneman-Tversky Optimization（KTO）的 HALO，用来直接最大化生成的效用，而不是像现有方法那样最大化偏好的似然。尽管只从一条输出是否（不）可取的二元信号中学习，KTO 在我们的实验里仍不差于、甚至好于基于偏好的方法。更广泛地说，我们的工作表明，正如不存在一个普遍更优的奖励模型，也不存在一个普遍更优的损失函数——最好的 HALO 取决于对给定场景最合适的归纳偏置，而要为每种情境找出最好的 HALO，还有很多工作要做。

10.text: When human feedback is in a binary format, and especially when there is an imbalance between the number of desirable and undesirable examples, KTO is the natural choice. When your data is in the form of preferences, the choice is less clear. Putting aside the greater data efficiency of KTO, our theoretical analysis suggests that if your preference data has sufficiently little noise and sufficiently little intransitivity, then DPO will work better, since there is some risk of KTO underfitting; this risk can be mitigated by using a lower value of β and aligning with KTO for more epochs. 11.text: The methods discussed in this paper have the potential to make LLMs more helpful and safer, which is often needed for models deployed in production. It is possible that in making models more helpful, we increase the utility of one person at the expense of broader society. In aligning models with human feedback, one may also—without even fully recognizing it—be aligning to an unrepresentative subset of the population, which may hinder the ability of individuals outside that subset to benefit equally from using the model. The data used for LLM alignment, including the datasets used in this paper (e.g., SHP, HH, OASST) contain preferences of groups that are not representative of the broader population. Biases in this data have the potential to be propagated downstream when used to align models with methods like KTO, especially when no efforts are made to adjust for the different population. KTO in particular implicitly resolves contradictions in feedback by favoring the majoritypreferred outcome for a loss-neutral value function, which does not comport with many theories of fairness (e.g., Rawlsianism). Since user preferences are, in turn, affected by the models they interact with, this also risks the homogenization of preferences and utility functions when KTO-aligned models are deployed at scale. The design of HALOs that resolve contradictions in more diverse ways is an important direction for future work. On the other hand, because KTO works with binary feedback, which is more abundant, cheaper, and faster to collect in the real world, it significantly lowers the barrier to data collection. This makes it easier to collect feedback from traditionally under-represented groups and serve different models to different users, instead of just one monolithic model being served to everyone.
11.zh: 本文讨论的方法有潜力让 LLM 更有用、也更安全，而这往往是部署到生产中的模型所需要的。在让模型更有用的同时，也可能以更广泛社会的利益为代价，提高某一个人的效用。用人类反馈对齐模型时，人们也可能——甚至没有充分意识到——是在向人口中不具代表性的一个子集对齐，这会妨碍该子集之外的人从使用模型中同等受益。用于 LLM 对齐的数据，包括本文使用的数据集（例如 SHP、HH、OASST），包含的是并不代表更广泛人群的群体偏好。这些数据中的偏差，在用 KTO 这类方法对齐模型时有可能向下游传播，尤其是在没有努力针对不同人群做调整的时候。KTO 尤其会隐含地消解反馈中的矛盾：对损失中性的价值函数，它偏向多数派更偏好的结果，而这与许多公平理论（例如罗尔斯主义）并不相符。由于用户偏好又会反过来受他们所交互的模型影响，当 KTO 对齐的模型大规模部署时，这也有使偏好和效用函数同质化的风险。设计能以更多样方式消解矛盾的 HALO，是未来工作的一个重要方向。另一方面，因为 KTO 使用二元反馈，而二元反馈在真实世界里更充足、更便宜、采集更快，它显著降低了数据采集的门槛。这使得更容易从传统上代表性不足的群体收集反馈，并为不同用户提供不同模型，而不是只向所有人提供一个单一模型。

14.text: Model Alignment as Prospect Theoretic Optimization
14.zh: 模型对齐作为前景理论优化

14.text: Human feedback has been used to improve LLM capabilities in translation (Kreutzer et al., 2018), summarization (Stiennon et al., 2020), sentiment-conditioned generation (Ziegler et al., 2019), and instruction-following (Ouyang et al., 2022). The RLHF framework (Christiano et al., 2017; Bai et al., 2022) traditionally used to accomplish this is detailed in §2. Still, momentum has largely shifted in favor of closed-form losses that directly operate on offline preferences, such as DPO (Rafailov et al., 2023). This single stage of optimization distinguishes DPO from the conventional approach in preference-based RL, which learns a reward and then fits the policy to those rewards (Jain et al., 2013; Busa-Fekete et al., 2014). Other preference-based losses include CPO (Xu et al., 2024) and IPO (Azar et al., 2024).
14.zh: 人类反馈已被用来提升 LLM 在翻译（Kreutzer et al., 2018）、摘要（Stiennon et al., 2020）、按情感条件生成（Ziegler et al., 2019）和指令遵循（Ouyang et al., 2022）上的能力。传统上用来完成这些的 RLHF 框架（Christiano et al., 2017; Bai et al., 2022）详见 §2。不过，势头已经明显转向直接作用在离线偏好上的闭式损失，例如 DPO（Rafailov et al., 2023）。这单一阶段的优化，把 DPO 和基于偏好的 RL 的常规做法区分开来；后者先学习一个奖励，再让策略去拟合这些奖励（Jain et al., 2013; Busa-Fekete et al., 2014）。其他基于偏好的损失包括 CPO（Xu et al., 2024）和 IPO（Azar et al., 2024）。

14.text: Despite not being a human-aware loss, unlikelihood training was among the first methods to align language models using a binary signal (Welleck et al., 2019). However, Korbak et al. (2023) found unlikelihood training to be worse than the CSFT baseline we tested in this work, which is among various approaches that convert a binary/discrete signal into a control token (Lu et al., 2022). Learning from sparse binary feedback is a staple of information retrieval and recommender systems (He et al., 2017; Koren et al., 2009). Many retrieval-augmented generation systems use contrastive learning to ensure that generations are grounded. This can be framed as learning from synthetic binary feedback, although depending on the implementation, it may be the retriever and not the LLM that is updated (Lu et al., 2022).
14.zh: 尽管不是人类感知损失，非似然训练是最早用二元信号来对齐语言模型的方法之一（Welleck et al., 2019）。不过 Korbak et al.（2023）发现非似然训练不如我们在本文中测试的 CSFT 基线，而 CSFT 属于把二元或离散信号转换成控制 token 的多种做法之一（Lu et al., 2022）。从稀疏二元反馈中学习，是信息检索和推荐系统的看家本领（He et al., 2017; Koren et al., 2009）。许多检索增强生成系统用对比学习来保证生成有据可依。这可以看成从合成二元反馈中学习，不过取决于实现，被更新的可能是检索器而不是 LLM（Lu et al., 2022）。

14.text: A recent string of work has centered on the idea of “self-training” or “self-play”, during which the policy is continually aligned on online data sampled from itself and then filtered (Chen et al., 2024; Yuan et al., 2024). Many of these approaches frame the learning of a preference model as a two-player min-max game between two policies (Munos et al., 2023; Rosset et al., 2024; Swamy et al., 2024). In theory, KTO can also be adapted for online alignment, though we leave this as a direction for future work.
14.zh: 最近一串工作围绕「自训练」或「自对弈」展开：策略不断在从自身采样、再经过筛选的在线数据上对齐（Chen et al., 2024; Yuan et al., 2024）。其中许多方法把偏好模型的学习刻画成两个策略之间的二人极小极大博弈（Munos et al., 2023; Rosset et al., 2024; Swamy et al., 2024）。理论上 KTO 也可以改造成在线对齐，不过我们把这留给未来工作。

14.text: Prospect theory, despite being influential in behavioral economics, has had a muted impact in machine learning, with work concentrated in human-robot interaction (Kwon et al., 2020; Sun et al., 2019; Chan et al., 2021).
